text: We moved to Ledgerly last year. Receipt matching still breaks whenever a merchant name on the card is different from the receipt, so someone fixes it by hand every week.
Ledgerly is fine for cards but month-end close still takes our finance person three days because the export to our accounting software drops the tax codes.
Crashes on upload. The app crashes every time I upload more than two receipts at once, which is exactly what I need to do after a trip.
Love how fast it is. Snapping a receipt takes two seconds and it is usually matched before I put my phone away.
Great support team. Support answered in ten minutes and fixed our card limit issue the same day.
Honestly the approval flow is the best part of Ledgerly. Managers approve from Slack and nobody chases anyone by email anymore.
The per-seat pricing gets painful fast. We pay for every employee who submits one expense a year, which feels wrong for a 60 person company.
Ledgerly raised prices on our renewal by almost forty percent. We are now looking at alternatives because the per-seat pricing does not fit how we use it.
I wish Ledgerly had per diem support. Our field team travels every week and we still calculate per diems in a spreadsheet.
Please add a proper CSV export with custom columns. Our auditor asked for a format Ledgerly simply cannot produce.
We left Northbook because the month-end close took a full week. Every expense needed manual coding before it could go to the accounting software.
Northbook is cheap and the cards work, but the approval flow lives in email and approvals get stuck for days when a manager is travelling.
Northbook support is slow. We waited four days for an answer about a blocked card while an employee was abroad.
The Northbook app is simple and reliable. It never crashed once in two years, which is more than I can say for other tools.
Quillsum has the best accounting sync I have seen. Approved expenses show up in the ledger with the right tax codes every time.
Quillsum is powerful but setup took us six weeks and a consultant. It is built for companies much bigger than us.
We switched from Quillsum after the price increase. Paying enterprise prices for a 30 person team made no sense anymore.
Quillsum receipt matching is very good but the mobile app is slow to open and people stopped using it.
Our biggest pain with expense tools is month-end close. Finance spends days chasing missing receipts before the books can close.
Missing receipts are the real problem. Half our team forgets to upload receipts until the end of the month and finance has to chase them.
We tried three expense tools and every one of them had broken receipt matching for foreign merchants with different names on the card.
I am hesitant to add another tool to onboard. Every new finance tool means training forty people who only submit expenses twice a year.
We are worried about migrating two years of expense history. Nobody wants to lose the audit trail when switching tools.
The moment we hit thirty employees the spreadsheet broke. Approvals got lost and nobody knew who had spent what.
Our auditor flagged that we could not show who approved each expense. That was the moment we switched to a real expense tool.
Per-seat pricing is the worst model for expense tools. Most employees submit a handful of expenses a year but you pay for all of them.
What I want is simple: card, receipt, approval, done. Getting expenses into the accounting software with the right codes is the job.
The job of an expense tool is to make the books close faster. Everything else is a nice extra.
Matching is hit and miss. Receipt matching works for big merchants but fails for small restaurants and taxis, so I do those by hand.
We picked Ledgerly over Quillsum because setup took one afternoon. That mattered more to us than any feature.
The analytics dashboards look nice but nobody on our team has opened them since the demo.
Month-end close is faster with Ledgerly than with spreadsheets, but the accounting sync still needs manual fixes for tax codes.
